item.title: X-MoE-4D: Breaking the Scaling Barrier for Trillion-Parameter MoEs on Hierarchical HPC Systems
item.description: X-MoE, the previously largest scale of MoE training shown on the Frontier HPC system, achieves only 10.2 TFLOP/s per GPU (5.3 % model FLOPs utilization, MFU) for 545 billion parameters on 1,024 GPU dies (GCDs), showing a strong limitation in scaling up large-scale MoE training on Frontier. In this work, we study the scaling bottleneck on the Frontier system, and we propose an alternative scaling pathway. In this blog, we present X-MoE-4D, which scales out MoE training via intra-node expert parallelism (EP) and inter-node pipeline parallelism (PP). X-MoE-4D further pushes the limits of trainability on HPC clusters to 1-trillion-parameter MoE models, achieving 24.8 % MFU on 960 GCDs. Its throughput is 2.24 times that of X-MoE on 1,024 GCDs. On a 173-billion-parameter model, X-MoE-4D maintains 36 % MFU in weak scaling up to 1,152 GCDs, and in strong scaling to 2,304 GCDs it is 3.24 times faster than X-MoE on 2,048 GCDs. The paper is accepted to SC 2026, and the code is available in the X-MoE repository.

item.title: X-MoE: Scaling DeepSeek-style MoEs on Frontier—what broke, what we fixed, and what to learn
item.description: This blog presents the background and key optimizations behind X-MoE, along with our hands-on experience scaling MoE model training on Frontier, the AMD GPU supercomputer.
